findings_addressed.oracle: Independent count oracle: len(report.process_activity) is computed before calling generate_timeline; the process-filtered timeline length must equal that count. A mutation dropping _timeline_add_process_events or silently skipping records changes the count and turns the assertion red.
findings_addressed.documented_mutation: In src/intellicrack/sandbox/analysis.py, delete the line `_timeline_add_process_events(report, events)` inside generate_timeline (around line 589) — process_only becomes [] while expected_process_event_count > 0, making `assert len(process_only) == expected_process_event_count` fail.

notes: The conditional-never-runs anti-pattern (N6 variant) was: `if report.process_activity: assert process_only`. On a real Windows capture process_activity is always non-empty so the assertion always ran, but the conditional guard meant a vacuous pass was possible if process_activity happened to be empty. The fix: (1) assert report.process_activity is non-empty as a hard precondition with a diagnostic message, (2) independently count expected process events before calling generate_timeline, (3) unconditionally assert len(process_only) == expected_process_event_count as a count oracle, removing the conditional guard entirely. The sort oracle and filter oracle (all events have category==process) are retained.
